subject: VAPA
title: Theatre & Performing Arts
description: A year-long introduction to theatre as both art form and craft. Students build ensemble and improvisation skills, train voice and body, learn Stanislavski-based acting technique through monologues and scenes, survey theatre history from ancient Greece to contemporary American and Latinx theatre, explore technical design, write and devise original short plays, and culminate in a directed one-act production for a live audience. Students keep a performance journal and write formal play critiques.
framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools – Theatre (High School Proficient); 2020 California Arts Education Framework

standards.TH:Cr1.1.HSI: Apply basic research to construct ideas about the visual composition of a drama/theatre work; explore physical, vocal, and physiological choices to develop a performance.
standards.TH:Cr2.1.HSI: Explore the function of history and culture in the development of a dramatic concept through a critical analysis of original ideas; investigate collaborative roles.
standards.TH:Cr3.1.HSI: Practice and revise a devised or scripted drama/theatre work using theatrical staging conventions; refine technical design choices.
standards.TH:Pr4.1.HSI: Examine how character relationships assist in telling the story; shape character choices using given circumstances.
standards.TH:Pr5.1.HSI: Practice various acting techniques to expand skills in a rehearsal or performance; use researched technical elements to increase the impact of design.
standards.TH:Pr6.1.HSI: Perform a scripted drama/theatre work for a specific audience.
standards.TH:Re7.1.HSI: Respond to what is seen, felt, and heard in a drama/theatre work to develop criteria for artistic choices.
standards.TH:Re8.1.HSI: Analyze and compare artistic choices developed from personal experiences and cultural contexts in multiple drama/theatre works.
standards.TH:Re9.1.HSI: Examine a drama/theatre work using supporting evidence and criteria while considering art forms, history, culture, and other disciplines.
standards.TH:Cn10.1.HSI: Investigate how cultural perspectives, community ideas, and personal beliefs impact a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.1.HSI: Explore how cultural, global, and historic belief systems affect creative choices in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.2.HSI: Research how other theatre artists apply creative processes to tell stories in a devised or scripted drama/theatre work, using theatre research methods.

units.title: Ensemble and Improvisation
units.big_idea: Theatre begins with trust, listening, and saying 'yes, and' to a scene partner.

units.title: Voice and Movement
units.big_idea: An actor's body and voice are instruments that must be trained to communicate clearly and expressively.

units.title: Acting Technique and the Monologue
units.big_idea: Truthful acting comes from playing objectives against obstacles within given circumstances.

units.title: Theatre History: Greece to Shakespeare
units.big_idea: Theatre's conventions grew from the beliefs and playing spaces of each culture and era.

units.title: Scene Study and Winter Showcase
units.big_idea: Scenes come alive when partners listen and react truthfully to each other.

units.title: American Realism and Diverse Voices
units.big_idea: American playwrights used realism and new forms to examine family, society, and identity.

units.title: Technical Theatre and Design
units.big_idea: Sets, lights, costumes, and sound are storytelling tools that must serve the production concept.

units.title: Playwriting and Devised Theatre
units.big_idea: Original theatre grows from personal and community stories shaped by dramatic structure.

units.title: Directing and Final Production
units.big_idea: A production unites actors, designers, and director in a shared interpretation for a live audience.

days.title: What is theatre?
days.work: Discuss what makes theatre different from film; set up a performance journal with goals for the year.

days.title: Focus games
days.work: Play mirror, Zip-Zap-Zop (with family), and 'counting to 20' focus games; journal what improved concentration.

days.title: Trust & physical awareness
days.work: Practice trust walks, neutral stance, and space-walking with tempo changes 1–10.

days.title: Group storytelling
days.work: Build a one-word-at-a-time story and a tableau series of a fairy tale in three frozen images.

days.title: Reflect & check
days.work: Perform a 3-tableau story for family and write a journal reflection on ensemble skills.

objectives: Apply 'yes, and' and CROW (character, relationship, objective, where)

days.title: Yes, and
days.work: Practice 'yes, and' vs. 'yes, but' dialogues and identify blocking offers.

days.title: CROW
days.work: Improvise 2-minute scenes establishing character, relationship, objective, and where within the first 30 seconds.

days.title: Status
days.work: Explore high- and low-status physical and vocal choices in short scenes.

days.title: Short-form games
days.work: Play Freeze, Three-Line Scene, and Party Quirks; journal which choices worked.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform three improvised scenes from audience suggestions and self-evaluate with a CROW rubric.

days.title: Leading centers
days.work: Explore walking led by head, chest, belly, and knees; create a character from each.

days.title: Animal work
days.work: Observe an animal (pet or video) and transform its movement into a human character.

days.title: Hot seating
days.work: Answer interview questions in character for 5 minutes.

days.title: Character monologue
days.work: Improvise a 1-minute character monologue built from a costume piece.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform two contrasting improvised characters and write a character profile.

days.title: Story spine
days.work: Learn the story spine ('Once upon a time... until finally') and improvise five stories.

days.title: Callbacks
days.work: Practice linking scenes with recurring characters and callbacks.

days.title: Watch & respond
days.work: Watch a professional improv clip and write a response identifying offers and callbacks.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a 10-minute structured long-form piece with family or friends.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Perform the long-form piece and complete a written reflection on Unit 1 growth.

days.title: Breath
days.work: Practice diaphragmatic breathing lying down with a book on the abdomen; sustain an 's' sound for time.

days.title: Resonance
days.work: Explore chest, mask, and head resonance with humming and sirens.

days.title: Articulation
days.work: Drill 10 tongue twisters at increasing speeds and record before-and-after clips.

days.title: Projection
days.work: Deliver a short poem to a partner at 5, 15, and 30 feet without shouting.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a vocal warm-up routine you designed and a 1-minute poem reading; compare to the week 1 recording.

objectives: Use Laban efforts and physical storytelling

days.title: Laban efforts
days.work: Explore the eight Laban efforts (punch, float, glide, slash, etc.) through movement improvisation.

days.title: Mime
days.work: Practice mime illusions (wall, rope pull, weight) and create a 1-minute mime scene.

days.title: Physical storytelling
days.work: Watch a clip of a physical theatre company and identify techniques.

days.title: Neutral mask
days.work: Explore neutral movement and a character arc without words.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a 2-minute wordless physical theatre piece with a clear beginning, middle, and end.

weeks.topic: Voice and body together: dialects and choral speaking
materials: choral text (e.g., Whitman excerpt or Greek chorus ode)

days.title: Pitch & inflection
days.work: Read a neutral sentence ten ways to convey different subtexts.

days.title: Dialect awareness
days.work: Listen to the International Dialects of English Archive samples and discuss respectful use of dialect.

days.title: Choral speaking
days.work: Arrange a Greek chorus excerpt or Whitman poem for multiple voices with movement.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse the choral piece focusing on unison, contrast, and staging.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Perform the choral piece and complete a voice and movement self-assessment.

days.title: Stanislavski
days.work: Read an overview of Stanislavski's system and the 'magic if'.

days.title: Objectives & tactics
days.work: Play an improvised scene where you must get a partner to open a door using five different tactics.

days.title: Given circumstances
days.work: Analyze who, what, where, when, why for a short scene from Chekhov's The Proposal.

days.title: Beats
days.work: Break a 1-page scene into beats and label each with an active verb.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on Stanislavski terms and a scored scene analysis.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Read 10 age-appropriate monologues and choose a contemporary or classical piece.

days.title: Read the play
days.work: Read the full play the monologue comes from and write the given circumstances.

days.title: Scoring
days.work: Score the monologue with beats, tactics, operative words, and pauses.

days.title: Memorization
days.work: Memorize using chunking and walking rehearsal.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform off-book for family and receive feedback.

days.title: Moment before
days.work: Improvise the moment before the monologue and connect it to the opening line.

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the monologue with purposeful movement and a focal point.

days.title: Video review
days.work: Record and analyze your performance with a rubric.

days.title: Coaching
days.work: Work with a coach or family member on specific notes.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a refined version and write a rehearsal journal entry.

objectives: Perform a monologue for an audience

days.title: Slating
days.work: Learn to slate (name and piece) and practice audition etiquette.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Run the monologue twice with notes.

days.title: Performance
days.work: Perform the monologue for an audience and record it.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Watch a professional monologue and write a critique using criteria.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Self-assess performance video and set goals.

objectives: Explain the origins of Western theatre

days.title: Origins
days.work: Read about the Festival of Dionysus and the structure of a Greek theatre.

days.title: Antigone
days.work: Read key scenes of Antigone and discuss conflict between law and conscience.

days.title: Masks
days.work: Make a Greek tragedy mask and explore how masks change movement.

days.title: Chorus
days.work: Stage a chorus ode with unison movement.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on Greek theatre and a perform-the-chorus showing.

weeks.topic: Medieval, commedia dell'arte, and world traditions

days.title: Medieval theatre
days.work: Read about mystery and morality plays and pageant wagons.

days.title: Commedia
days.work: Learn stock characters (Arlecchino, Pantalone) and their physical lazzi.

days.title: Commedia scene
days.work: Improvise a commedia scenario with stock characters.

days.title: Asian traditions
days.work: Watch Noh and kabuki clips and compare conventions with Western theatre.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a comparison of two traditions.

materials: Folger Shakespeare text of A Midsummer Night's Dream

days.title: Globe
days.work: Explore the Globe Theatre and Elizabethan staging conventions.

days.title: Verse
days.work: Scan lines of iambic pentameter and speak them aloud.

days.title: Text work
days.work: Paraphrase a Shakespeare speech and identify operative words.

days.title: Insults & sonnets
days.work: Perform a sonnet with attention to rhythm.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a short Shakespeare speech.

objectives: Perform a Shakespeare scene with a partner
materials: Folger text of A Midsummer Night's Dream

days.title: Casting & reading
days.work: Choose the mechanicals' rehearsal (Act 3.1) or the lovers' quarrel (Act 3.2); read it aloud and paraphrase each line.

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the scene on a taped-out stage, marking entrances, crosses, and asides in the script.

days.title: Comic timing
days.work: Rehearse for comic timing, practicing pauses before punchlines and physical bits.

days.title: Watch & compare
days.work: Watch the same scene in two filmed versions (e.g., 1999 film and a Globe stage recording) and chart differing choices.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Perform the scene and take the Unit 4 theatre history test (Greek through Elizabethan).

objectives: Analyze and rehearse a contemporary two-person scene
materials: two-person scene from a contemporary play (library collection)

days.title: Choose scene
days.work: Read three two-person scenes, choose one with a partner, and read the full play it comes from.

days.title: Table work
days.work: Write the given circumstances, each character's objective, and the relationship history.

days.title: Repetition exercise
days.work: Practice the Meisner repetition exercise for 15 minutes to train listening and impulse.

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the scene so that every cross is motivated by a tactic change.

days.title: Check
days.work: Run the scene off-book and write a journal entry on one moment that felt truthful.

objectives: Refine scenes and monologues for an audience

days.title: Polish
days.work: Work the three highest-stakes moments of the scene and monologue with a coach, raising stakes and clarifying transitions.

days.title: Props & costumes
days.work: Choose simple costume pieces and props that reveal character; create a prop list.

days.title: Program & publicity
days.work: Design a printed program with bios and a poster inviting family and friends.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Run the full showcase (monologue, Shakespeare scene, contemporary scene) in costume.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Receive and apply notes; rehearse curtain call and transitions between pieces.

days.title: Final rehearsal
days.work: Run the full show once at performance pace, including the curtain call.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Perform the winter showcase for invited family and friends and record it.

days.title: Video review
days.work: Watch the recording and log three strengths and three growth areas using the acting rubric.

days.title: Written reflection
days.work: Write a 500-word semester reflection citing specific moments from the video.

days.title: Semester exam
days.work: Written exam on acting terms, Stanislavski, and theatre history from Greece to Shakespeare.

days.title: Realism
days.work: Read about Ibsen, Chekhov, and the rise of realism and the fourth wall; read a scene from A Doll's House.

days.title: Trifles reading
days.work: Read Trifles aloud by roles and list the clues the women find.

days.title: Subtext
days.work: Analyze subtext in the women's dialogue and write what each line really means.

days.title: Scene work
days.work: Rehearse the final scene of Trifles with attention to silence and small gestures.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform the scene and write a paragraph on how Glaspell uses objects to tell the story.

days.title: Act I
days.work: Read Act I and discuss Wilder's use of the Stage Manager and bare stage.

days.title: Pantomime
days.work: Practice pantomiming everyday tasks (making breakfast, stringing beans) with precise detail.

days.title: Act III
days.work: Read Act III and discuss Emily's speech 'Do any human beings ever realize life?'

days.title: Staging
days.work: Stage Emily's goodbye speech with no set and minimal props.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform and compare Wilder's presentational style with Glaspell's realism in writing.

weeks.topic: Diverse American voices: Hansberry, Valdez, and Wilson
objectives: Investigate cultural perspectives in American theatre
materials: Lorraine Hansberry, A Raisin in the Sun excerpt
Luis Valdez, Las Dos Caras del Patroncito (acto)

days.title: Teatro Campesino
days.work: Learn about Luis Valdez and El Teatro Campesino's actos performed for striking farmworkers in Delano.

days.title: Acto
days.work: Read and rehearse Las Dos Caras del Patroncito with masks and placards.

days.title: Hansberry & Wilson
days.work: Read excerpts from A Raisin in the Sun and Fences; compare family conflicts.

days.title: Research
days.work: Research one playwright of color and the community their work speaks for.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present a 4-minute research talk with a short performed excerpt.

objectives: Write a formal theatre critique using criteria
materials: a full filmed or live production (local theatre, community college, or streaming)

days.title: Model reviews
days.work: Read two professional theatre reviews and identify their structure and criteria.

days.title: Attend
days.work: Attend a live local production or watch a full filmed play; take notes on acting, design, and direction.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft a 700-word critique evaluating three production elements with specific evidence.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for precise theatre vocabulary and balanced judgment.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Submit the critique and take a short quiz on American theatre.

objectives: Design a set for a scene

days.title: Stage types
days.work: Compare proscenium, thrust, arena, and black box stages with diagrams.

days.title: Script analysis
days.work: Analyze Trifles for every set requirement implied by the text.

days.title: Ground plan
days.work: Draw a 1/4-inch scale ground plan for the Trifles kitchen.

days.title: Model box
days.work: Build a shoebox model of the set.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present the model and explain how it supports the mood.

objectives: Use light and sound to create mood

days.title: Light qualities
days.work: Experiment with intensity, color, and angle using flashlights and cellophane on a face.

days.title: Light plot
days.work: Create a simple cue sheet with 8 lighting cues for a short scene.

days.title: Sound
days.work: Find or record sound effects and underscore for a scene.

days.title: Sound cue sheet
days.work: Write a sound cue sheet with timings.

days.title: Check
days.work: Run a scene with your light and sound cues for family.

days.title: Research
days.work: Research the historical period of a chosen play.

days.title: Renderings
days.work: Draw costume renderings for three characters.

days.title: Costume plot
days.work: Create a costume plot by scene.

days.title: Makeup
days.work: Practice basic stage makeup (contour, aging) on yourself.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present a costume design portfolio.

days.title: Concept
days.work: Write a production concept statement for the one-act you will produce in Unit 9.

days.title: Collage
days.work: Build a visual research collage (mood board).

days.title: Design meeting
days.work: Present ideas in a mock design meeting.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise design based on feedback.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Submit design portfolio and take a technical theatre quiz.

objectives: Use dramatic structure in original writing

days.title: Structure
days.work: Map Freytag's pyramid onto Trifles, labeling the inciting incident, turning points, and climax.

days.title: Dialogue only
days.work: Write a 1-page scene using only dialogue in which two characters want the same object; no stage directions allowed.

days.title: Play format
days.work: Learn standard play format (character names, parentheticals, stage directions) and reformat your scene.

days.title: Character design
days.work: Create two original characters with a want, a fear, and a secret; write a 1-paragraph bio for each.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit a 3-page scene draft putting the two characters in conflict.

objectives: Write and revise a complete ten-minute play

days.title: Idea
days.work: Brainstorm 10 premises from personal, family, or community stories; pick one with a clear conflict and a single setting.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Outline the play in 6–8 beats with the turning point placed around minute 7.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Write the full 8–10 page draft.

days.title: Table read
days.work: Hold a table read with family or friends, recording it and noting where listeners lost interest.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise using the recording, tightening dialogue and clarifying the climax; submit the second draft.

objectives: Collaboratively create a devised piece from source material

days.title: Devising companies
days.work: Watch clips about Tectonic Theater Project (The Laramie Project) and Frantic Assembly; list their devising methods.

days.title: Source gathering
days.work: Interview two community members on a shared theme (e.g., 'home') and collect found text.

days.title: Viewpoints
days.work: Explore Viewpoints (tempo, spatial relationship, repetition) to generate movement material.

days.title: Composition
days.work: Combine verbatim lines and movement into three short compositions.

days.title: Showing
days.work: Shape the compositions into a 6–8 minute piece and show it for feedback.

objectives: Present original work in a staged reading

days.title: Casting & rehearsal
days.work: Cast your ten-minute play with family/friends and rehearse it as a staged reading.

days.title: Polish
days.work: Refine stage-direction reading and transitions; finalize the devised piece.

days.title: Festival
days.work: Present the staged reading and devised piece to an audience.

days.title: Talkback
days.work: Lead a talkback using Liz Lerman's Critical Response Process and record feedback.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a 400-word reflection on what you learned as a playwright and deviser.

weeks.topic: The director's role and play selection
objectives: Select and analyze a one-act play
materials: public-domain one-acts (e.g., Glaspell's Trifles, Chekhov's The Proposal, Wilde excerpts)

days.title: The director
days.work: Read about the history of the director and watch an interview with a working director.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Read three public-domain one-acts and choose one for production, considering cast size and audience.

days.title: Script analysis
days.work: Analyze the chosen play's structure, characters, and themes in a prompt book.

days.title: Concept
days.work: Write a director's concept statement linking to the design concept from Unit 7.

days.title: Casting
days.work: Hold auditions with family/friends or a homeschool co-op and post a cast list.

days.title: Stage areas
days.work: Review stage areas and blocking notation; mark the floor plan with tape.

days.title: Pre-block
days.work: Pre-block the first half of the play in the prompt book.

days.title: Rehearsal 1
days.work: Block the first half with actors, adjusting for sightlines.

days.title: Rehearsal 2
days.work: Block the second half and record blocking in the prompt book.

days.title: Run
days.work: Hold a stumble-through of the full play and give notes.

days.title: Schedule
days.work: Build a rehearsal schedule to performance week with an off-book deadline.

days.title: Character work
days.work: Lead an actor workshop on objectives for each character.

days.title: Scene work
days.work: Work two key scenes for pacing and stakes.

days.title: Off-book run
days.work: Hold the off-book run and track line errors.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Practice giving specific, actionable notes and write a rehearsal report.

materials: set pieces, costumes, lights, sound from Unit 7 designs

days.title: Build
days.work: Build or gather the set, props, and costumes from the design portfolio.

days.title: Cue-to-cue
days.work: Run a cue-to-cue rehearsal for lights and sound.

days.title: Costume parade
days.work: Hold a costume parade and fix problems.

days.title: Tech run
days.work: Run the play with all technical elements.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Write production notes and fix issues.

objectives: Perform a one-act production for a live audience

days.title: Dress rehearsal 1
days.work: Run the full play in costume with timing notes.

days.title: Dress rehearsal 2
days.work: Final dress with an invited preview audience.

days.title: Performance 1
days.work: Perform the one-act for an audience.

days.title: Performance 2
days.work: Perform a second time and record it.

days.title: Strike
days.work: Strike the set and return materials.

days.title: Video review
days.work: Watch the production video and log strengths and growth areas.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Write a 600-word self-critique of the production using theatre criteria.

days.title: Artistic statement
days.work: Write an artistic statement about what theatre means to you.

days.title: Portfolio
days.work: Assemble a digital portfolio with headshot, résumé, monologue video, design work, and play.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take a written final on theatre terms, history, and production roles.
